questions.question: How many female superheroes have a strength value of 100?
questions.evidence: female refers to gender = 'Female'; strength value of 100 refers to attribute_name = 'Strength' AND attribute_value = 100
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN attribute AS T3 ON T2.attribute_id = T3.id INNER JOIN gender AS T4 ON T1.gender_id = T4.id WHERE T3.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND T2.attribute_value = 100 AND T4.gender = 'Female'

questions.question: Which superhero has the most durability published by Dark Horse Comics?
questions.evidence: which superhero refers to superhero_name; most durability refers to MAX(attribute_value) WHERE attribute_name = 'durability'; published by Dark Horse Comics refers to publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics';
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN attribute AS T3 ON T3.id = T2.attribute_id INNER JOIN publisher AS T4 ON T4.id = T1.publisher_id WHERE T4.publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics' AND T3.attribute_name = 'Durability' ORDER BY T2.attribute_value DESC LIMIT 1

questions.question: List the superheroes from Marvel Comics who have the super power of 'Super Strength'.
questions.evidence: the superheroes from Marvel Comics refers to publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'; super power of "Super Strength" refers to power_name = 'Super Strength';
questions.SQL: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS T2 INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id WHERE T3.power_name = 'Super Strength' AND T1.id = T2.hero_id)AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS T4 WHERE T4.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND T1.publisher_id = T4.id)

questions.question: Which publisher published the slowest superhero?
questions.evidence: the slowest superhero refers to attribute_name = 'Speed' where MIN(attribute_value); publisher refers to publisher_name
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.publisher_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T3 ON T1.id = T3.hero_id INNER JOIN attribute AS T4 ON T3.attribute_id = T4.id WHERE T4.attribute_name = 'Speed' ORDER BY T3.attribute_value LIMIT 1

questions.question: Find the ratio between male superheroes and female superheroes.
questions.evidence: ratio = DIVIDE(SUM(gender_id = 1) / SUM(gender_id = 2)); male superheroes refers to gender = 'Female'; female superheroes refers to gender = 'Male';
questions.SQL: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.gender = 'Male' THEN T1.id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) / COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.gender = 'Female' THEN T1.id ELSE NULL END) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN gender AS T2 ON T1.gender_id = T2.id

questions.question: State all of 3-D Man's attributes along with their values.
questions.evidence: 3-D Man is the superhero_name. attributes refers to attribute_name; values refers to attribute_value;
questions.SQL: SELECT T3.attribute_name, T2.attribute_value FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN attribute AS T3 ON T2.attribute_id = T3.id WHERE T1.superhero_name = '3-D Man'

questions.question: What is Copycat's race?
questions.SQL: SELECT T2.race FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN race AS T2 ON T1.race_id = T2.id WHERE T1.superhero_name = 'Copycat'

questions.question: Among the male superheroes, list the super hero names of superheroes with weight greater than the 79% average weight of all superheroes.
questions.evidence: super hero names refers to superhero_name;male superheros refers to gender = 'Male';Calculation = weight_kg > MULTIPLY(AVG(weight_kg), 0.79)
questions.SQL: SELECT T1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN gender AS T2 ON T1.gender_id = T2.id WHERE T2.gender = 'Male' AND T1.weight_kg * 100 > ( SELECT AVG(weight_kg) FROM superhero ) * 79

questions.question: Give the publisher ID of Star Trek.
questions.SQL: SELECT id FROM publisher WHERE publisher_name = 'Star Trek'

questions.question: Calculate the difference between Emil Blonsky's weight and Charles Chandler's weight.
questions.evidence: difference = SUBTRACT(SUM(weight_kg WHERE full_name = 'Emil Blonsky'), SUM(weight_kg WHERE full_name = 'Charles Chandler')); Emil Blonsky is the full name of superhero; Charles Chandler is the full name of superhero;
questions.SQL: SELECT ( SELECT weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE full_name LIKE 'Emil Blonsky' ) - ( SELECT weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE full_name LIKE 'Charles Chandler' ) AS CALCULATE

questions.question: Which superheroes have a durability attribute value of less than 50?
questions.evidence: durability of less than 50 refers to attribute_name = 'Durability' AND attribute_value < 50
questions.SQL: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_attribute AS T2 INNER JOIN attribute AS T3 ON T2.attribute_id = T3.id WHERE T3.attribute_name = 'Durability' AND T2.attribute_value < 50 AND T1.id = T2.hero_id)

questions.question: Between DC and Marvel Comics, which publisher has published more superheroes? Find the difference in the number of superheroes they have published.
questions.evidence: DC refers to publisher_name = 'DC Comics'; Marvel Comics refers to publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'; calculation = SUBTRACT(SUM(publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'), SUM(publisher_name = 'DC Comics'))
questions.SQL: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN T2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN T2.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id

questions.question: What is the average weight of all female superheroes?
questions.evidence: female refers to gender = 'Female'; average weight refers to AVG(weight_kg)
questions.SQL: SELECT AVG(T1.weight_kg) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN gender AS T2 ON T1.gender_id = T2.id WHERE T2.gender = 'Female'

questions.question: How many green-skinned villains are there in the superhero universe?
questions.evidence: green-skinned refers to colour.colour = 'Green' WHERE skin_colour_id = colour.id; villains refers to alignment = 'Bad';
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN alignment AS T2 ON T1.alignment_id = T2.id INNER JOIN colour AS T3 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T3.id WHERE T2.alignment = 'Bad' AND T3.colour = 'Green'

questions.question: How many heroes have the highest attribute value in strength?
questions.evidence: highest attribute value in strength refers to MAX(attribute_value) WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength';
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.hero_id) FROM hero_attribute AS T1 INNER JOIN attribute AS T2 ON T1.attribute_id = T2.id WHERE T2.attribute_name = 'Strength' AND T1.attribute_value = ( SELECT MAX(attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute )

questions.question: Among the superheroes with the super power of "Super Strength", how many of them have a height of over 200cm?
questions.evidence: super power of "Super Strength" refers to power_name = 'Super Strength'; a height of over 200cm refers to height_cm > 200
questions.SQL: SELECT COUNT(T1.id) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN hero_power AS T2 ON T1.id = T2.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id WHERE T3.power_name = 'Super Strength' AND T1.height_cm > 200

questions.question: Among the superheroes with height from 170 to 190, list the names of the superheroes with no eye color.
questions.evidence: height from 170 to 190 refers to height_cm BETWEEN 170 AND 190; no eye color refers to colour = 'No Colour'
questions.SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN colour AS T2 ON T1.eye_colour_id = T2.id WHERE T1.height_cm BETWEEN 170 AND 190 AND T2.colour = 'No Colour'

questions.question: What are the superpowers of heroes with ID 1?
questions.evidence: superpowers refers to power_name; heroes with ID 1 refers to hero_id = 1;
questions.SQL: SELECT DISTINCT T2.power_name FROM hero_power AS T1 INNER JOIN superpower AS T2 ON T1.power_id = T2.id WHERE T1.hero_id = 1
